newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-MCRAE OUTSPRINTS SAINZ IN DRAMATIC FINALE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE OUTSPRINTS SAINZ IN DRAMATIC FINALE.

text.p: Briton Colin McRae took every conceivable risk on Wednesday to beat Spaniard Carlos Sainz and win the Tour of Corsica.

The 1995 champion, who had started the last day of the rally in fourth position 22 seconds behind the Spaniard's Ford Escort, clocked the best time in three of the final six timed stages for a brilliant victory.
Before the final section, over 34.33 kms from Stiliccione to Marati, in the mountains south of Ajaccio, McRae was second seven seconds behind Sainz.
But he confirmed he was a formidable competitor with aggressive driving on wet asphalt to gain 15 seconds on his rival in that stretch alone.
"I would have preferred dry conditions because we didn't do much testing with the rain tyres but it was okay," said McRae. "I didn't have much choice anyway. My only option was to attack."
Sainz had to settle for second place overall eight seconds behind while Frenchman Gilles Panizzi came third a further 30 seconds back in his Peugeot 306.
"I didn't know that last timed stage very much and I think Colin's tyres were better than mine for wet roads," said Sainz. "Never mind, it was a great battle. I hope it was fun to watch."
There was bitter disappointment for Panizzi's team mate and compatriot Francois Delecour, who shared the lead with Sainz overnight.
Hampered by a wrong choice of tyres and clutch problems, Delecour lost ground to end up fourth 55 seconds behind the leader.

McRae, who had been looking for a win since taking the Safari Rally in Kenya last March, retained second place in the world championship standings but is now only two points behind leader Tommi Makinen of Finland.
World champion Makinen crashed out of the rally when his Mitsubishi Lancer bumped into a cow on Tuesday. He has 28 points to McRae's 26.
McRae's victory made up for a frustrating run in last month's Catalunya rally, where he was fighting for the lead when a puncture forced him to drop to fourth place.
This year's Tour of Corsica, made particularly tricky by changing weather conditions with occasional downpours, was marked by another fine perfomance from the lightweight, two-wheel drive Peugeots.
As in the Catalunya rally, where they led for much of the opening day before Panizzi eventually finished third, the Puegeots matched the massive four-wheel drive cars.
Panizzi was in the lead after the first day on Monday and on Tuesday, Delecour and Panizzi were joint first and third respectively.
"The choice of tyres was the most difficult thing in this rally," said Panizzi. "What McRae did is just fantastic but I think we can be proud of what we've achieved."
